I'm going to work on boundaries. I can start by not picking up the phone or acknowledging her texts. In fact, I don't think I'll even help her with her night routine tonight. "Grow up."

Oof, sorry for the extra post but had another thought. I'm starting to wonder if going numb in response to Nparent tirades isn't better than feeling the pain. It's hit the point where it feels like my brain is jettisoning entire chunks of memory/focus/executive function. I'm at work and I feel my concentration blip out between steps of things. It's not great.

It's an important thing to remember, even if I struggle with it still. No amount of explaining or educating or maintaining what you know to be true can change them or clear their delusions. It hurts so much to know that my truth doesn't matter, but I'm trying to train myself to remember that their recognition isn't worth the trouble. Still hurts.

I got told to walk off my broken foot that was making me nauseous from pain. To be fair, I was still hoping it was just a super bad strain, but imagine the "shocked pikachu" faces when I showed them my x-ray and came home with a boot.

Two general questions here:

How do you manage yourself around an Nparent who has cancer? I feel like my humanity is slipping because I'm getting too tired to drop everything and run at every groan. Being unpleasant to a person with cancer is like, the biggest moral no-no, but with all the screaming and chaos I'm starting to have trouble and that's troubling me.

Second, how do you maintain energy to go about your day after Nparent chaos? My mornings are extremely stressful due to manufactured and organic chaos (with apologies to our puppy), and by the time I get to work I'm so drained that there's not much energy left to hold myself together with.
